name: Groom and triage new issues
description: A maintainer opens an issue; issue-groom runs om-auto-manage-issues (SDLC labels, the Definition of Ready check, implementation notes) and then afk-triage (an Agent Brief, or `blocked` with a comment naming what a person must do), in one run so the two never race on the same labels (ADR 0017, ADR 0029). `authors` is the gate: both steps hold Bash with no allowlist and read the issue body, so an issue from anyone else is never groomed by automation. Every agent files its issues as `rafalwolak` too (one identity, no bot account), and that is intended: a follow-up afk-triage or afk-architecture-review files is groomed and triaged here like any other, and afk-triage stops at once on an issue that already carries an Agent Brief. Issues a run holds or a person put on hold never match.

name: Re-triage when a hold is cleared
description: A person removes `blocked` from an issue - the thing it waited on is done or answered - and issue-groom grooms and triages it again, so the issue reaches an Agent Brief without anyone starting a run (ADR 0029). Same `authors` gate as above.

name: Implement the next ready issue
description: Every two hours implement-ticket takes the one highest-priority, oldest ready issue - opened by the maintainer, carrying an Agent Brief, a category, a priority and a risk, with every "Blocked by" issue closed, no open or merged-unclosed PR and no `blocked`, `do-not-merge`, `do-not-close` or `in-progress` - as `node .ai/scripts/backlog-status.mjs --next` picks it, implements it test-first, gates it, opens the PR and drives it through review, QA and CI to the merge into develop by om-pr-autopilot --allow-merge (ADR 0027, ADR 0029). The script answers nothing while three agent PRs are open, so one tick starts at most one issue and the queue never outruns review. `risk-high` and `security` issues are not skipped: implement-ticket re-derives the risk from the area and claims one only on the security and tenancy specialist's approving verdict (SDLC.md § Delegated decisions), and a `risk-high` PR waits for the owner's `qa-approved`. A schedule rather than an event: a ticket becomes ready when its blockers close, and no GitHub event says so.

task.prompt: Implement the next ready issue in {{project}} ({{date}}).

name: Autopilot new pull requests
description: A PR opened as `rafalwolak` gets om-pr-autopilot, which diagnoses it and runs the right chain through to the merge into develop (ADR 0027). There is one GitHub identity: every agent PR is authored by `rafalwolak` too, so the author filter only keeps dependabot and outside contributors out. Agent PRs are told apart by their pipeline labels instead: om-open-pr opens one carrying `review` inside its own chain (implement-ticket, issue-autofix), so `excludeLabels` stands down on `review` and every later pipeline label rather than race that chain. The standing develop-to-main promotion PR is opened with the owner's token too, and no filter here reads the base branch, so .github/workflows/promote-develop.yml opens it carrying `do-not-merge`, which is excluded: an unattended run never touches the release (ADR 0029).

name: Merge reviewed agent pull requests
description: A PR that om-auto-review-pr approved into `merge-queue` gets om-pr-autopilot --allow-merge, which merges it into develop through om-approve-merge-pr (ADR 0027). A backstop for the implement chain, which drives its own PR to the merge: a reviewed PR whose chain ended early is picked up here. `authors` stays: every agent PR is authored by `rafalwolak`, and the filter keeps dependabot and outside contributors out - the housekeeping sweep (om-review-prs) can approve their PRs into `merge-queue`, and this run reads the PR as a prompt while holding Bash with no allowlist. `merge-queue` tells agent PRs apart from the rest. The develop-to-main promotion PR carries `do-not-merge` and never `merge-queue`, so it never matches (ADR 0029).

name: Spec to tickets
description: Weekday mornings: afk-to-tickets slices at most one newly merged spec into vertical tickets, each carrying its Agent Brief in the body. Schedule rather than an event, so it never races the issue pipeline above. A ticket with no open blocker is ready at once, and "Implement the next ready issue" takes it; the rest become ready as their blockers close (ADR 0029). Idempotent - a spec that already has a parent issue is skipped.

task.prompt: Run the afk-to-tickets skill for {{project}} on {{date}}: slice at most one unsliced spec.

name: Weekly architecture review
description: Mondays: afk-architecture-review reads the last 30 days of hot spots and files at most three refactor issues, each with a recommendation strength. Read-only on code - the only writes are issues, which "Groom and triage new issues" then grooms and briefs like any other, and a judgement call is settled by a specialist sub-agent (`.ai/skills/afk-decide/SKILL.md`). It reads `.ai/skills/afk-codebase-design/SKILL.md` for its vocabulary - the shared half, kept identical by hand across the repositories that use this pipeline - and this repository's own seams are in the override beside it.

task.prompt: Run the afk-architecture-review skill for {{project}} on {{date}}.

name: Weekly lessons
description: Fridays: afk-lessons turns mistakes repeated across the last 14 days of pull requests into enforced rules - mechanical ones into a lint rule, judgement into CODE_REVIEW.md, operational into AGENTS.md. A lesson seen only once is not a rule, so a quiet fortnight is a no-op, and it opens at most one pull request per run.

task.prompt: Run the afk-lessons skill for {{project}} on {{date}}.
